questions.question_text: A potted plant is kept in darkness for two days before an experiment on starch production. What is the main purpose of this step?
questions.option_a: To remove all chlorophyll from the roots
questions.option_b: To make the stomata permanently open
questions.option_c: To use up previously stored starch so later starch can be linked to the experimental treatment
questions.option_d: To increase the plant’s mineral uptake
questions.explanation: Destarching reduces starch already stored in leaves, so starch found after the experiment can be attributed to conditions during the test.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After a destarched leaf is exposed to light, iodine turns part of it blue-black. Which substance does this colour indicate?
questions.explanation: Iodine forms a blue-black complex with starch; the leaf is first decolourised to make the test visible.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Two destarched plants are placed under identical light; one is enclosed with potassium hydroxide that absorbs carbon dioxide. The enclosed plant’s leaf fails the starch test. Which variable was shown necessary?
questions.explanation: KOH absorbs carbon dioxide; failure to form starch under otherwise similar conditions supports the requirement for CO2 in photosynthesis.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A variegated leaf is exposed to light and then tested for starch. Only the green regions turn blue-black. What conclusion is best supported?
questions.option_a: Light prevents starch formation in green tissue
questions.option_c: Chlorophyll-containing regions are where starch was produced in this test
questions.option_d: Starch is produced only in roots
questions.explanation: Starch appears in illuminated green regions, supporting the role of chlorophyll-containing tissue in photosynthesis.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A tracer experiment labels oxygen atoms in the water supplied to a plant. The labelled oxygen appears in the oxygen released during photosynthesis. What does this show?
questions.option_a: Released oxygen originates only from carbon dioxide
questions.option_b: Water supplies no atoms to photosynthesis
questions.option_c: Released oxygen originates from water splitting
questions.option_d: Oxygen release is unrelated to light reactions
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water during the light reactions releases oxygen; isotope tracing identifies water as its source.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A crop maintains photosynthesis relatively well in hot, bright conditions because carbon dioxide is concentrated around Rubisco in bundle-sheath cells. Which pathway is being used?
questions.explanation: C4 plants initially fix CO2 into four-carbon compounds and concentrate CO2 near Rubisco, reducing photorespiration in hot, bright environments.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A succulent plant takes in carbon dioxide mainly at night and uses stored acids during the day. Which adaptation is illustrated?
questions.explanation: CAM plants open stomata at night and store carbon in organic acids, conserving water during hot daytime conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: With light and carbon dioxide held at adequate levels, photosynthesis rises as temperature increases and then falls sharply above an optimum. Which explanation best accounts for the fall?
questions.option_a: Chlorophyll permanently becomes an animal pigment
questions.option_b: Photosynthetic enzymes lose activity at excessively high temperature
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis depends on enzymes; high temperatures can impair enzyme structure and function, reducing the rate after an optimum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A plant develops interveinal chlorosis first in older leaves. Which deficiency is especially plausible because magnesium is mobile and is part of chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is the central ion in chlorophyll and can be remobilised from older leaves; deficiency commonly causes chlorosis.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A crop shows stunted growth and purplish older leaves in a soil test-confirmed low-phosphate field. Which deficiency best fits?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is needed for ATP and nucleic acids; deficiency can restrict growth and produce dark or purplish foliage.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A young leaf shows interveinal chlorosis while older leaves remain greener. Which mineral deficiency is consistent with the limited mobility of the nutrient within many plants?
questions.explanation: Iron is relatively immobile in many plants; deficiency often appears as chlorosis in young leaves.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fungus colonises a plant’s roots and increases the effective soil volume from which phosphate can be absorbed. What association is this?
questions.explanation: Mycorrhizal fungi associate with roots and can improve uptake of phosphate and water from soil.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A legume’s root nodules contain bacteria that convert atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable compounds. Which bacterium is classically associated with this process?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen into compounds that can enter plant and soil nitrogen cycles.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a well-aerated soil, microbes oxidise ammonium first to nitrite and then nitrate. Which nitrogen-cycle process is occurring?
questions.explanation: Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonium to nitrite and then nitrate, which many plants can absorb.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Waterlogged soil becomes oxygen-poor and nitrate levels fall as microbes release nitrogen gas. Which process accounts for this change?
questions.explanation: Denitrifying microorganisms reduce nitrate to gaseous nitrogen compounds, returning nitrogen to the atmosphere, especially in low-oxygen soils.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A plant cannot use atmospheric nitrogen gas directly for most of its growth. What must generally happen first?
questions.option_a: The plant must digest atmospheric nitrogen with enzymes in the stomach
questions.option_b: Nitrogen must be fixed into usable compounds such as ammonium or nitrate
questions.option_c: Nitrogen gas must be converted into oxygen by leaves
questions.option_d: Nitrogen must be changed into glucose in chloroplasts
questions.explanation: Most plants assimilate nitrogen as inorganic compounds such as ammonium or nitrate; atmospheric N2 must first be fixed by biological or industrial processes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A cereal-based diet is supplemented with pulses. Why can this improve the quality of dietary protein?
questions.option_a: Cereals contain no protein at all
questions.option_b: Both foods supply only non-essential amino acids
questions.option_c: Pulses convert all carbohydrate into vitamin C
questions.option_d: The amino-acid patterns of cereals and pulses can complement one another
questions.explanation: Cereal and pulse proteins often have complementary limiting essential amino acids, improving the overall amino-acid pattern when eaten together.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person cannot synthesise a particular amino acid in sufficient quantity and must obtain it from food. How is that amino acid classified?
questions.explanation: Essential amino acids cannot be made in adequate amounts by the body and must be obtained through diet.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A diet contains equal masses of fat and carbohydrate. Which statement about their potential energy yield is generally correct?
questions.option_a: Carbohydrate supplies about twice as much energy as fat
questions.option_b: Both provide identical energy per gram
questions.option_c: Neither nutrient can be oxidised for energy
questions.option_d: Fat supplies more energy per gram than carbohydrate
questions.explanation: Fat yields about 9 kcal per gram, while carbohydrate provides about 4 kcal per gram.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A child has night blindness after prolonged inadequate intake of certain vegetables and animal foods. Which nutrient is most directly implicated?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed for normal visual pigments; deficiency can impair dim-light vision.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient’s gums bleed easily and wounds heal poorly after a diet lacking fresh produce. Which biochemical role links the deficiency to these symptoms?
questions.option_a: Vitamin A is required for haemoglobin synthesis
questions.option_c: Vitamin C is required for collagen formation
questions.option_d: Vitamin D forms the clotting mesh
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is required for collagen synthesis; deficiency can produce scurvy, including gum changes and impaired wound healing.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An older adult has bone softening and low calcium absorption after little sunlight exposure and inadequate dietary intake. Which vitamin deficiency is a likely contributor?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D supports calcium and phosphate absorption and normal bone mineralisation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A diet dominated by polished rice is associated with weakness and nerve symptoms. Which missing nutrient is classically implicated?
questions.explanation: Thiamine deficiency can cause beriberi, which may affect nerves and the cardiovascular system.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person with a very restricted diet develops dermatitis, diarrhoea and cognitive changes. Which deficiency syndrome should be considered?
questions.option_a: Night blindness from vitamin A deficiency
questions.explanation: Pellagra is caused by niacin deficiency and classically includes dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pattern correctly describes vitamin solubility and storage tendency?
questions.option_a: All vitamins are water-soluble and immediately excreted
questions.option_b: A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and can be stored; most B vitamins and C are water-soluble
questions.option_c: Only vitamin C can be stored in body fat
questions.option_d: B-complex vitamins are fat-soluble while A and D are water-soluble
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble; most B vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble. Fat-soluble vitamins can accumulate in tissues.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person with severe protein deficiency has muscle wasting and oedema, while calorie intake is not as low as in severe starvation. Which condition is most consistent?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is associated with severe protein deficiency and oedema; marasmus is marked by severe overall energy deficiency and wasting.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A child has profound wasting and loss of body fat after prolonged inadequate energy intake. Which form of malnutrition is most likely?
questions.explanation: Marasmus results from severe energy deficiency, often with protein deficiency, and causes marked wasting.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A diet has sufficient calories but very little indigestible plant material. Which outcome is most directly associated with low fibre intake?
questions.option_c: Reduced stool bulk and increased risk of constipation
questions.option_d: Impaired oxygen transport from low haemoglobin
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre adds bulk and supports bowel movement; low intake can contribute to constipation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A laboratory tests an unknown food sample with Biuret reagent and observes a violet colour. Which nutrient class is indicated?
questions.explanation: Biuret reagent turns violet in the presence of peptide bonds, indicating proteins.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A blood sample has impaired synthesis of several clotting factors in a patient with low intake of a fat-soluble vitamin. Which vitamin is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is required for the activation of several blood-clotting proteins; it is fat-soluble.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
